research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 14006 of January 26, 2021, Reforming Our Incarceration System To Eliminate the Use of Privately Operated Criminal Detention Facilities (86 FR 7483, PDF pages 1-2 of the 2021-01-29 issue, FR Doc. 2021-02070), matching the census register row (2021-01-26, Joseph R. Biden Jr.). I read the whole held text; the page identification is taken from the held text's own header, not from a page image. Inventory: the dossier's seven scopes (sec1, sec2, sec3, sec3-i, sec3-i-ii, sec3-b, sec3-c) run from section 1 to section 3(c) and the signature, and no operative sentence lies outside them; I confirm the inventory without change. The order has one operative command, section 2 (the Attorney General is not to renew Department of Justice contracts with privately operated criminal detention facilities, as consistent with applicable law), with no deadline, condition, sunset, report or term. Ending: Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025, section 2(q), lists this order among the executive actions that are 'are hereby revoked:' It has no delayed-effect wording and no exception or saving for this order, so every scope ended on its signing date, January 20, 2025; the alternative reading, its Federal Register publication on January 28, 2025, would only move the date. The by-number search of held texts (the six texts in the packet lookups are four copies of EO 14148 and two of this order) and the three machine searches found no statute, court action, expiry or other instrument acting on this order, so the revocation is the first end of every scope and the whole-order end. The OLRC note at 18 U.S.C. 4013 note reports the same revocation. The order was therefore not operative on the 2026-10-14 cutoff; provisional status NO is unchanged. The original is the official FR text layer; no working-text substitute is used.
